title: The Song Celestial, or Bhagavad Gita
author: Edwin Arnold (trans)
description: The Song Celestial, or Bhagavad-Gita (from the Mahabharata), Sir Edwin Arnold's verse translation first published in 1885, being a discourse between Arjuna, Prince of India, and the Supreme Being under the form of Krishna. Arnold, author of The Light of Asia, rendered the 700-verse Sanskrit poem into flowing English blank verse and lyric metres. It was through this translation that the young Mohandas Gandhi first read the Gita in London. On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Arjuna despairs at fighting his kinsmen, and Krishna teaches him in eighteen chapters on the immortal Self, duty (dharma), the yoga of selfless action, knowledge and devotion, the nature of Brahman and the three gunas, and reveals his universal cosmic form. The Gita is the most influential text of Hindu spirituality, central to Vedanta and to Theosophy, Transcendentalism and modern yoga.
